title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 24 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and maritime & undersea autonomy.

stories.h: Neros to expand domestic drone production with $450M Pentagon loan
stories.what: The company is a frontrunner in a Defense Department competition to find the best quality, most affordable small drone for combat.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: Ukraine moves to create its own Space Force
stories.what: Ukraine’s parliament has taken the first step toward creating a Space Force within the country’s armed forces. On November 9, the Verkhovna Rada approved in the first reading draft law No.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.what: Declaring that the fundamental duty of America's armed forces is to assure victory in war, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said the nation's senior service colleges must have a curriculum that underpins that duty during a speech at the U.S. Naval War College.
stories.you: Budget and policy moves decide which programs get real money and when; they're the earliest signal of demand.

stories.h: The next breakthrough is software built on the battlefield by agentic bots
stories.what: [Sponsored] Autonomous agents and mission-specific software promise faster responses to emerging threats.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: Firm bets on converted fishing trawlers to tackle Russian submarines in the Arctic
stories.what: The company’s Arctic Hunter idea involves an industry-standard 56-meter trawler design whose fish-processing innards are ripped out and replaced with autonomy features.
stories.you: What China, Russia and Iran field sets the requirements the Pentagon buys against.

watch.why: November 10. Could squeeze drone, motor and munitions supply weeks before the DoD ban.

idea.why: Licenses combat-proven Ukrainian designs (ground robots, interceptors, software) and handles compliance and US or EU production. About 300 Ukrainian ground-drone firms and 500 FPV makers are looking for export routes; Brave1 is certifying exports.
